description: A single fully visible XRD panel, labelled (a), of a low-carbon low-density cryogenic steel, plotted as Intensity (a.u.) on the y-axis (gridlines 10000-60000, curves vertically offset for clarity) against 2θ (°) on the x-axis from 40 to 100° with ticks every 10°. Five offset diffractograms are colour-coded in the top-right legend: purple 0%, green 3%, blue 10%, red 28% and black 55%. Reflections are indexed (111)γ near 50.5°, (110)α near 52.5°, (200)γ near 59.5° and (220)γ near 89.5°, i.e. a dominant fcc austenite (γ) pattern with a weak bcc ferrite (α) (110) line. The (111)γ peak of the 0% curve rises above the 50000 gridline; the (110)α peak is clearly resolved on the 0% (purple) pattern but is much weaker on all other patterns. Printed austenite fractions sit beside each curve: 95.6%γ (0%), 97.3%γ (3%), 95.7%γ (10%), 96.8%γ (28%) and 96.1%γ (55%). The panel therefore demonstrates that the γ fraction stays essentially constant (all within ~2 percentage points) across the five labelled conditions, while the residual ferrite signal almost disappears away from 0%. The right edge is cropped, a partial neighbouring panel label being visible; the caption text supplied is only "Table 4", which does not describe this diffractogram.

A cropped neighbouring panel label (a partial parenthesis at the top-right corner) and a sliver of the next panel; too little is visible to identify its content.

observations.observation: Five vertically offset XRD curves are distinguished by a legend in the top-right: purple 0%, green 3%, blue 10%, red 28%, black 55%.
Peaks are indexed as (111)γ (about 50.5°), (110)α (about 52.5°), (200)γ (about 59.5°) and (220)γ (about 89.5°), indicating an austenite (γ) fcc phase with a ferrite (α) (110) reflection.
The (110)α ferrite peak is clearly present in the 0% (purple) pattern and is markedly weaker on the 3%, 10%, 28% and 55% patterns.
Austenite fractions printed beside the curves are 95.6%γ (0%), 97.3%γ (3%), 95.7%γ (10%), 96.8%γ (28%) and 96.1%γ (55%).
Across the five labelled conditions the γ fraction varies only from 95.6% to 97.3%, i.e. within about 2 percentage points.
The y-axis is Intensity (a.u.) with gridlines at 10000-60000 and the x-axis is 2θ (°) spanning 40-100° with ticks at 10° intervals.
The (111)γ peak of the 0% curve is the most intense feature, rising above the 50000 gridline, whereas the corresponding peaks of the other curves stay below the 30000 gridline.
A partial label at the top-right corner is cut off, showing that this diffractogram is only one panel of a multi-panel figure.
The supplied caption text is only 'Table 4' and contains no description, units, or conditions, so it does not describe the XRD pattern shown in the pixels.
